clue.text: Newspaper's connected to underworld — they deflect the heat?

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; with the possessive it gives the letters SUNS
Hades is the Greek underworld, the realm of the dead

explanation.surface: A tabloid is linked to the criminal underworld, and asked whether its staff deflect the heat of police attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The heat' in the surface suggests police pressure on a crooked paper; in the definition it is just hot sunshine. The Sun is a British daily tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasols and awnings shield people from hot sunlight, which is what the questioning definition describes.

clue.text: Ice in the second half of the weekend, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.words: the second half of the weekend
parts.note: the weekend is Saturday then the Lord's day

explanation.surface: Ice is said to feature late in the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter is unchecked: the sound gives the day, the spelling is the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-cream dessert topped with syrup and nuts; ice is an old word for ice cream.

clue.text: Piece contributing to compilation one thousand

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece forms part of a collection of a thousand puzzles, fitting this milestone edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical composition for nine players or voices is a piece of music.

clue.text: Stockings girl's heard about leading to exclamations of praise

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, the sound giving a different spelling

parts.note: stockings are hose, and a girl's could be Anna's

explanation.surface: A girl's stockings are reported to have prompted cries of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about leading to' is link material: the hose and Anna's said together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts of adoration in worship, as in Palm Sunday cries to God, are cries of praise.

clue.text: Finished off dad's untended patio, finally rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters are put together again in a new shape
finally takes the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Father's neglected patio has at last been reconstructed and completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes O from 'patio', and 'rebuilt' rearranges it with DADS UNTENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely finished and dealt with.

clue.text: Dispatched exhausted, having lost power

indicators.note: having lost says a letter is removed from the word for exhausted

parts.note: spent means tired out
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone tired out is sent away after losing their strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Something posted or sent off has been dispatched.

clue.text: Brick carrier, note, returned

indicators.note: returned says the note's letters come back the other way

parts.note: doh is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A builder's worker carries bricks, takes a note, and sends it back.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder's trough on a pole, carried on the shoulder, holds bricks or mortar.

clue.text: Piping filmed for expert

parts.note: piping hot means very hot
a scene filmed is shot

explanation.surface: Bagpipe playing was recorded for a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly skilled, successful person is informally an ace.

clue.text: Lastly, had you take on an extra governess

indicators.note: Lastly applies to every word that follows, taking each one's final letter

explanation.surface: Finally, you had to take on an additional children's tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lastly' looks like a sentence adverb; it is the signal to take the ends of the six following words.
explanation.definitionFit: An older woman acting as chaperone and governess to girls, especially in Spain.

clue.text: Fools grandmothers

definitions.meaning: a nana is informal British slang for a silly person
nana is a familiar word for a granny

explanation.surface: Older relatives are made fun of as silly.
explanation.definitionFit: One informal word covers both a foolish person in British slang and a child's name for a grandmother.

clue.text: Girl, initially not available, almost caught

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words that follow
almost means the last letter is dropped from the word for caught

parts.note: a fish caught is netted

explanation.surface: A young woman was nearly snared after first being unavailable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' works on both 'not' and 'available', giving the abbreviation N/A; 'almost' cuts the D from NETTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanette is a female given name, made famous by the musical No, No, Nanette.

clue.text: They receive an unfinished banknote outside front of ATM

indicators.note: outside says the shortened note wraps around the next piece
unfinished drops the final letter of the word for the banknote

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of the cash machine's abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone gets a ten-pound note not quite fully dispensed outside a cash machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They receive' looks like people collecting cash; it is aerials picking up signals. 'unfinished' trims the banknote, and 'front of' takes one letter from ATM.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerials on a radio or television pick up signals, so they are things that receive.

clue.text: Ignore informal parade ground command

definitions.meaning: to snub or avoid someone deliberately
the drill sergeant's clipped cry of 'attention!'

explanation.surface: A soldier disregards a barked order on the drill square.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to avoid deliberately, and is also the shortened form of the bellowed military order to stand to attention.

clue.text: Minded accommodation for someone in South Sea resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort says the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone looked after lodgings for a friend at a seaside holiday spot in the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place; read as re-sort it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after another person's home while they are away is to mind their accommodation.

clue.text: Stands on odd roundabout giving advice

indicators.note: roundabout suggests things going round and round, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stands on a peculiar traffic circle while offering guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of rules about what to do and avoid is practical guidance.

clue.text: Way to serve cheese, perhaps, and one short health drink?

indicators.note: short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a toast is a drink to someone's health

explanation.surface: A recipe suggests a cheese dish, and a quick one, with a drink for wellbeing.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'health drink' sounds like a smoothie; it is a toast, drunk to someone's health.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese or beans may be served on a slice of grilled bread, a standard way of presenting it.

clue.text: Hudson runs around barefoot

indicators.note: runs around suggests letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone named Hudson dashes about without shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Without shoes, especially of a horse not shod, means barefoot.

clue.text: Fellow's keeping odd bits of non-fat dyes

indicators.note: keeping says the fellow's letters hold the next piece inside

parts.note: he is a fellow, so fellow's is he's

indicators.note: odd bits of picks the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A man keeps parts of a low-fat product and colours things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes N, N, A from NON-FAT. Here the answer is a verb: colours with a reddish plant dye.
explanation.definitionFit: To henna hair is to colour it with a reddish plant extract, so it dyes.

clue.text: Could be Hazel's crazy!

definitions.meaning: the fruits a hazel tree might bear

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a person called Hazel is out of her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name, but it is the tree, whose fruits are hazelnuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazelnuts grow on the hazel, and the same word is slang for mad.

clue.text: House, not unexpectedly, eclipsed

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A house was surprisingly overshadowed by something.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to surpass in brilliance, and the past tense of shining brighter than others means the same.

clue.text: Best to expose swindle

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: It is better to unmask a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them.

clue.text: Biblical brother cheated in games, audaciously

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A sibling from scripture was boldly cheated at play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheated' is a nod to the story: Jacob tricked his elder twin out of his birthright.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this hairy elder twin of Jacob sold his birthright for a bowl of stew.

clue.text: Teacher fixed equipment for language lab?

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
set means fixed or settled

explanation.surface: A teacher has set up the gear for a language laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Students in a language lab wear earphones with a microphone to listen and speak, hence the question mark example.

clue.text: Getting article on the day is the very devil!

indicators.note: on says the article comes after the day piece in this across answer

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Getting an item into the paper on the day itself is a real nightmare.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil himself is the prince of darkness, the very devil in person.

clue.text: Small girl's point

definitions.meaning: a pet form of Dorothy, short and so small

explanation.surface: A little girl makes her point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small girl' is a shortened girl's name; the 's is 'is', linking the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a short name for Dorothy and also a small round mark or spot.

clue.text: Thrown out unused, being far from reliable

indicators.note: thrown suggests letters tossed about and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: Something discarded unused turns out to be untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a rare, archaic word; once the crossing letters are in the anagram falls into place.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking in duty or obedience means not dependable, someone who cannot be trusted to do their part.
